endorsements.quote: Clinicians must verify and interpret AI-generated outputs within the context of professional expertise and patient care standards.
Clinicians should regard AI technologies as supplementary and supportive tools in clinical practice, ensuring they complement, rather than replace, clinical judgment.

To ensure responsible and sustainable adoption, institutions must establish comprehensive governance frameworks for AI across domains such as education, research, procurement, data management, and clinical operations ( 3 ).
The researcher must declare and document the use of AI technologies at each stage of the research process.

unlisted_practices: Integrate AI literacy and competency content into the undergraduate health professions curriculum, horizontally and vertically across educational stages.
Do not input confidential or personal data into AI systems beyond the organisation without the explicit consent of the relevant individuals.
Educators should outline in the course syllabus the scope and guidelines for using AI technologies and explain the rationale to students.
Researchers must review and validate the data and results generated by AI technologies for accuracy and relevance.
Dental professionals should critically evaluate the certification status of AI products before employing them for patient care.

screen.reason: Presents a competency framework and curriculum recommendations for training undergraduate dental students on AI.
